title: Read a Settlement Layout
definition: A place where people live and carry out connected activities.
content:
A settlement includes more than a collection of houses. Streets, open spaces, workplaces and public buildings connect peoples activities. Colonial planning changed some settlements, but a plan is not proof that every place was built or used identically. Ask how the arrangement related to the people living there and how it changed over time.

UNESCO describes Vigan in Ilocos Sur as a planned colonial town with a street grid and adjacent plazas. It also identifies Vigan as a trading place before Spanish rule. This named example connects earlier activity with later planning; it does not mean communities began only when colonial authorities arrived. Our diagram is a fictional layout model, not a measured map of Vigan. Trace a route between two places and ask what evidence would show actual daily use.

clues: Connected spaces
Streets and open spaces connect activities within a settlement.
Named example
Vigan had earlier trading activity as well as later colonial planning.
Plan limit
A model layout does not establish every residents route or every towns form.
task: A fictional town plan shows streets and open spaces. What can it directly help investigate?
How the depicted spaces connect, not every residents actual daily route
Every towns exact layout
Proof that communities began only under Spanish rule
The private beliefs of every resident
reason: How the depicted spaces connect, not every residents actual daily route. A model layout does not establish every residents route or every towns form.

title: A House Could Combine Materials
definition: A substance used to make part of a building.
content:
The term bahay na bato is often translated as stone house, but it should not make us imagine that every part was stone. NHCP guidelines describe regional house styles using masonry and wood, including stone lower portions and wooden upper floors in typical examples. Builders combined materials and skills rather than copying one unchanged design everywhere.

Try a fictional building card. It labels a masonry lower part and a wooden upper part. You can describe the combination without claiming it is an exact drawing of a named surviving house. A material label alone does not date construction, identify every maker or show who could afford such a house. Other housing forms also existed. Do not rank the worth of residents by their building materials. Compare particular houses with their setting, available materials and dated records.

clues: Combination
Bahay na bato examples can combine masonry and wood.

One house type does not describe every familys dwelling.

Examples could combine masonry and wood; check the particular building

reason: Examples could combine masonry and wood; check the particular building. One house type does not describe every familys dwelling.

title: Look for Light and Air
definition: The movement of air into and through a space.
content:
A building feature can help us ask how people used a space. UNESCO describes sliding window panels with kapis shells and wooden frames in Vigan houses, allowing more air when opened. This gives a concrete example of a feature connected with ventilation. It does not prove that every house used the same windows or that one feature solved every problem of heat and weather.

Our teaching diagram shows an open panel and an arrow for air movement. The arrow is a model, not a measured airflow test or instructions for changing a heritage building. Compare the closed and open positions. Then ask what the evidence supports: a possible function of the opening, rather than every residents comfort or an exact room temperature. Materials, maintenance, building arrangement and conditions all need investigation in a particular case.

title: Work and Home Could Share a Building
definition: The activities carried out in a building or part of it.
content:
Houses could connect domestic life with work and exchange. NHCP recognizes variation in house forms and functions. In a named Vigan example, UNESCO describes merchants using ground-floor spaces for shops, offices or storage, with living spaces above. That is a useful pattern to investigate, not a floor plan for every household or every century.

Our fictional cutaway separates a lower work area from an upper living area. It helps us ask how activities could connect. It cannot identify the people who used a particular room, prove that every resident was wealthy, or show every task done in a day. A later museum display may also arrange rooms differently from earlier residents. Compare dated plans, household records and accounts of use before presenting a complete story. The model does not invite entry into private houses or ask students for their home layout.

clues: Different activities
A building can contain both work and living spaces.

title: Buildings Have Histories Too
definition: Caring for heritage while keeping evidence of its history.
content:
A towns beginnings and a houses construction are different dates. A surviving house may include additions, repairs and changed uses. We need to investigate those stages rather than date every visible feature to the founding of a settlement. A photograph records an appearance at a time; it does not show all earlier forms.

A United Nations report describes documentation and expert assessments of Vigan houses after the 2022 earthquake, including the Syquia Mansion and Cabildo House. This modern conservation example shows why recording features before and during repair matters. It is not proof of a buildings exact colonial appearance. Our fictional timeline has construction, a later alteration and a modern repair. Keep each stage separate. Students can respect heritage and learn from records without climbing damaged structures, entering private spaces or attempting repairs.

Open the three clues and choose the explanation they support. Use Explain for help or return to the lesson before targeted practice if the topic needs review.
clues: Different dates
Settlement beginnings, construction, alteration and repair can belong to different periods.
Record before repair
Documentation helps keep evidence of features and changes visible.
Modern evidence
A conservation report is not automatic proof of every earlier appearance.
task: A town founding date is attached to every visible house feature. What should be checked?
Construction, alteration and repair dates for the particular features
Nothing because every feature must share one date
Only whether the building looks old
Whether all residents had identical beliefs
reason: Construction, alteration and repair dates for the particular features. A conservation report is not automatic proof of every earlier appearance.

title: Prepare Your Settlement and Housing Report
definition: Caring for heritage while keeping evidence of its history.
content: Review five ideas. Settlements connect places and activities. Houses could combine materials and local skills. Features such as openings helped people use spaces. Some buildings combined work with domestic life. Buildings also changed through construction, alteration, use and repair. A surviving town or house does not show every communitys experience. Prepare a fictional heritage report for another Grade 5 learner. Name a place or feature, give a supporting clue and explain what remains uncertain. Label the town plan and house cutaway as models. Do not use a towns beginning to date every later feature, or judge peoples worth from house materials. Keep local work visible and compare dated evidence before describing daily life. The main quiz has five questions, and three correct passes this mission. Review linked learning content before practice and a retry if needed. Complete all missions, then pass the chapter challenge to earn the chapter badge.
clues: Different dates
Settlement beginnings, construction, alteration and repair can belong to different periods.
Record before repair
Documentation helps keep evidence of features and changes visible.
Modern evidence
A conservation report is not automatic proof of every earlier appearance.
task: Which report best explains a historic house?
Describe features with dated evidence and identify model and source limits
Date every feature to the towns founding
Treat one house as every familys home
Rank people by their building materials
reason: Connect layouts, materials, functions and changes through dated evidence while recognizing variation.
